text: Which of these is the strongest reason to prefer an interface over an abstract class?
choices: Implementers may already have a superclass, and unrelated types can share the capability.
Interfaces can hold state, so they express more of the design than an abstract class can.
Interfaces dispatch faster, because they avoid the superclass method table entirely.
Abstract classes cannot declare methods that subclasses are required to implement.
explanation: Since Java 8 gave interfaces default and static methods the distinction narrowed, and what remains is state and the single-superclass budget. An interface costs an implementer nothing they may need elsewhere, and it lets `String` and `LocalDate` share `Comparable` despite having no common ancestor. Reach for an abstract class when implementations genuinely share state and code and are honestly kinds of one thing.
